posts.name: 35-world-third-kind-magnet
posts.caption:
Textbooks teach two kinds of magnet, and physicists now have strong X-ray evidence for a third kind called altermagnets 🧲

A SLAC led team fired left and right twisted X-rays at manganese telluride (MnTe) and saw a handedness signal an ordinary antiferromagnet should not produce. They repeated the test in 2025 with the same result. Caveat: one material, measured in deep cold, and the authors still call for sharper follow-up tests. Spintronic chips are a possibility, not a product.

Source: Jost et al. (SLAC National Accelerator Laboratory, Stanford, ESRF, University of Notre Dame), “Chiral Altermagnon in MnTe” (arXiv title), Science, 2026.
